full_text:
The NFL season is coming into view, which means more NFL player props are being released each week. Most national sportsbooks have posted 2026 NFL Player Props for Receiving Touchdowns for the top wide receivers and tight ends. In this article, I highlighted a bet I’ve already dropped in our Betting Discord and a couple of additional wagers I considered.

Wagering your hard-earned money in the summer and waiting more than half a year for bets to be settled isn’t the easiest pill to swallow. Nevertheless, if we can get the best of the lines before the markets fully mature in the future, it will make the wait until the end of the season worth it in the long run. Make sure to shop around for the best lines and odds if you have access to multiple sportsbooks. You’re likely to see more volatility between books on NFL Futures in the off-season than you’ll see on game lines and player props during the season. Let’s see if we can find some value in these lines for NFL Receiving Touchdowns.

Brolley’s Leans
---------------

##### __{{Justin Jefferson|WR|MIN|21685}}__ (Min) over 6.5 receiving TDs (-105, theSCORE Bet)

+ __Why I like the over__: Jefferson squeezed out his sixth consecutive 1000-yard season, despite a shaky 71.7% catchable target rate from J.J. McCarthy and company. He ranked sixth in target share (28.5%) and second in route share (93.5%), but scored just 2 TDs on 141 total targets (1.4%). He finished fifth with 13 end-zone targets last season, converting only 2 of those opportunities into touchdowns (15.4%). The Vikings actually finished second in pass rate over expectation inside the 5-yard line (10%) and third inside the 20-yard line (5%). His touchdown luck should regress if Kyler proves to be a significant upgrade at the quarterback position.

+ __Why I ultimately passed__: It will be shocking if Kyler isn’t an improvement over Minnesota’s near-league-worst quarterback play from 2025, but will he be a significant enough improvement to help Jettas score more TDs? Murray owns a career 4.1% TD rate and hasn’t topped a 3.9% TD rate in each of his last four seasons. Jefferson has scored 5 or fewer TDs twice in his last three seasons, despite being a perennial first-round fantasy pick since he stormed onto the scene as the 20th overall pick in 2020. He’s scored on 4.8% of his career targets (42 of 871), which is weaker than contemporaries like Ja’Marr Chase (7.0%), Amon-Ra St. Brown (5.9%), and CeeDee Lamb (4.9%).

##### __{{Rome Odunze|WR|CHI}}__ (Min) under 7.5 receiving TDs (-125, BetMGM)

+ __Why I like the under__: Odunze posted 6 TDs through 12 games but missed the final five games of the regular season with a stress fracture. He’s still dealing with complications from the break, [telling the media](https://apnews.com/article/chicago-bears-rome-odunze-edece1a9ebd209066f9925d58c493981) this spring that calluses have created a different type of foot structure after his fracture. The Bears ranked 23rd in pass rate over expectation inside the 5-yard line (-8.0%) and 29th inside the 20-yard line (-9.7%). Chicago could throw more in the scoring areas of the field, but Johnson’s offenses ranked 20th or lower in PROE from those areas of the field in each of his three seasons as the Lions playcaller.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: The Bears weren’t too concerned about Odunze’s injury situation when they moved on from DJ Moore and Olamide Zaccheaus without adding much to their receiving corps outside of Kalif Raymond. He has stiff competition to be the #1 receiver for Caleb Williams, but he’s the most proven target over Colston Loveland and Luther Burden. Odunze tied for 10th with 11 end-zone targets, converting just 2 of those opportunities (18.1%) into touchdowns. His luck could regress on those targets this season, especially if he’s a little healthier and if Williams improves his meager 69.4% catchable throw rate, which ranked 34th out of 38 passers.

##### __{{Tetairoa McMillan|WR|CAR|26054}}__ (Car) under 6.5 receiving TDs (-110, Bet365)

+ __Why I like the under__: McMillan is talented enough to reach double-digit TDs, but Bryce Young is too inconsistent to put my trust in Tet and this offense heading into 2026. Carolina scored a whopping 74.3% of its touchdowns on the ground last season, which should regress after 55% of their TDs came via the air in 2024. The Panthers easily led the league with a 16.4% pass rate over expectation from inside the 5-yard line last season, but they ranked 30th in PROE from outside the 5-yard line at -4.5%. Young is coming off a 4.8% TD rate thanks to Carolina’s pass-heavy approach near the goal, but he owns a meager 3.5% TD rate for his career.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: The NFL’s Offensive Rookie of the Year could continue his ascension after surpassing expectations as the eighth overall pick. Brett Whitefield placed Tet on the [Drake London/Mike Evans spectrum](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/2025/profiles/rookie/wr) as a prospect because of his short-area quickness and his ability to get out of breaks at 6’5”. Tet started to fill out his massive frame like Evans, who played at a listed weight of 231 pounds last season. McMillan said he added 17 pounds of muscle this offseason after playing at a listed 212 pounds as a rookie. That could make him even more of a menace near the goal line after tying for sixth in end-zone targets (12) and fourth in end-zone touchdowns.

##### __{{Travis Kelce|TE|KC|15048}}__ (KC) over 3.5 receiving TDs (-160, Bet365)

+ __Why I like the over__: You have to pay a little juice for this line, but Kelce has reached 4+ TDs in 11 of 12 seasons since becoming a full-time player in 2014. He’s also reached 15+ games played in every season since he underwent microfracture surgery after one game as a rookie in 2013. Kelce saw just 3 end-zone targets last season, which should regress after averaging 6.5 EZ targets in his previous four seasons. The Chiefs ranked second overall in pass rate over expectation (6.8%), and they attempted the third-most passes from inside the 5-yard line (28) and the sixth-most passes from inside the 20-yard line (91). Kelce could lead the Chiefs in targets for the fifth consecutive season if Rashee Rice can't stay healthy, gets suspended, or goes to jail (again).
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Kelce is a future Hall of Famer, but it’s fair to wonder how much he has left in the tank after he seemingly decided to play one more season because of his first losing season in 2025. He’s trending in the wrong direction heading into what is likely his final season before he runs off with his soon-to-be superstar wife. His efficiency continued to dip at 36 years old, averaging 1.67 YPRR and .21 TPRR on a 74% route share. Patrick Mahomes is coming off a major knee injury and no longer actively targets Kelce in the red zone. He’s gone under his season receiving touchdown line in three straight seasons, scoring just 13 TDs overall in that span.

##### __{{Mike Evans|WR|SF|16597}}__ (SF) over 5.5 receiving TDs (-120, theSCORE Bet)

\>Risk 1.2 units to win 1 unit. [Placed June 17](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/brolleys-best-bets-nfl-futures).

Evans bolted for San Francisco to chase a second Super Bowl, and he wants to add to his Hall-of-Fame resume with an upgrade at playcaller (__Kyle Shanahan__) and quarterback (__Brock Purdy__). He’s still a matchup nightmare at all three levels of the field because of his size (6’5”, 231 pounds), speed, and physicality even as he enters his age-33 season. He finished sixth in aDOT (14.1) and eighth in TPRR (.28) among 76 WRs who saw 50+ targets last season. He also ranked behind only __Davante Adams__ in A.S.S. (.147) — just ahead of OPOY __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ — but 67th in catchable target rate (67.8%) with __Baker Mayfield__ struggling through injuries under one-and-done playcaller __Josh Grizzard__.

He shouldn’t have the same issues with Purdy, who ranked fifth in catchable throw rate (78.9%), and under Shanahan, whose passing game finished behind only the Patriots in success rate (54.2%). Evans is playing with a new quarterback for the first time since 2022, when the Buccaneers switched from __Tom Brady__ to __Baker Mayfield__, but he has had no issues transitioning to new quarterbacks since entering the league in 2014.

He’s coming off his first season without 6+ touchdowns since the 2017 season, which was just the second time in 12 seasons that he failed to reach that mark. He scored just 3 times in eight games because of a hamstring injury and a broken clavicle, scoring on just 4.8% of his 62 targets. He previously posted a 7.3% TD rate through his first 11 seasons, scoring 105 times on 1431 targets. Evans should get plenty of opportunities to score in a 49ers offense that produced the fourth-most passing TDs (33) last season. San Francisco’s offense finished above league average in pass rate over expectation from the 20-yard line and in, including seventh (7.3%) from the 5-yard line and in. Purdy owns an elite 6.2% TD rate through four seasons, which ranks behind only __Lamar Jackson__ (6.5%) among active QBs.
